name: Rask
content:
LAGOM

rask — an agnostic multimodal lakehouse: Lance tables governed by a catalog, with lineage and authorization.

> ⚠️ **Work in progress — don't use.** *Lagom* is the Swedish word for "just the right amount" — not too little, not too much. It is the design rule for this platform: every tier governed, nothing over-built, and no capability that cannot say where its data came from. A **Lance lakehouse** under Lance Namespace (a governed REST catalog that enforces the bronze → silver → gold tiers in its write path, and OpenLineage provenance), **events** on Dapr + NATS JetStream, and **governance** over all of it — Dex OIDC for identity, OpenFGA for authorization, S3-compatible storage (RustFS in development, the platform's S3 in production). The lakehouse runs no ingest, no pipeline stage, no training and no workflow engine: compute and orchestration are the user's, and a pipeline writes every tier through the catalog's Lance Namespace doors like any other client (ADRs 0154 and 0155). **The platform is workload-agnostic by design.** It stores and governs blobs and multimodal data; no workload is its identity. Anything that reads bytes, writes a governed table and emits lineage fits the same shape — text, image, audio, video, embeddings. A workload's model, stage graph and output format are its own and live outside this repository; no shared seam (the catalog and its tier governance, the maintenance sweep, lineage, the events) names one. The test for any shared seam is *would this still be right for audio?* This repository holds the lakehouse and its console, nothing else. Every other client (flows, compute and the Ray engine fixtures, the annotator, the viewer and search with the explorer, table-maintenance, the sealed runners) left it and is recovered from git history at `64ef118a9`, the last commit that holds every client, when it moves to its own repository. Polyglot monorepo: Python via [uv], JS/TS via [Bun] (oxlint + oxfmt), docs via [Zensical], hermetic builds via [Dagger] (`.dagger/` — **every image**, local and CI). ## Layout Two language-pure planes: Python at the repo root, all JS/TS under `frontend/`. - `packages/` — reusable Python libraries (uv workspace members, no entrypoints): `service-kit` (the platform package a client pins by lakehouse tag: the app factory, the auth plane, the naming, and the contract the lakehouse's events publish), `lakehouse-kit` (the lakehouse's kernel, with `lakehouse_kit.storage`, its S3 client, STS and URI seam; no client imports it) and `lineage-kit` (OpenLineage emission and the Ed25519 signing seam) - `services/` — runnable Python services (uv workspace members): - **the lakehouse**: `catalog` (governed Lance REST catalog — projects → warehouses → namespaces → tables, and the bronze→silver→gold tier governance a pipeline's writes pass through), `lineage` (the OpenLineage intake, the commit feed and edge list as Lance tables, and the durable `GET /events` log; the lineage graph is bring-your-own, ADR 0158), `maintenance` (version expiry, trash purge, the orphan scan, cross-store reconcile, and the list of tables due for a bring-your-own compaction or index optimize; ADR 0162) - **the console's backend**: `notifications`, the per-subject inbox behind the console's bell, a client of the lakehouse's events (ADR 0190) - **the edge** is the platform's Gateway (Kubernetes Gateway API), not a rask process: the chart's HTTPRoutes (`chart/templates/route.yaml`) send each public `/api/*` prefix to its service, and every service authenticates each request itself (ADR 0165) - `frontend/` — the JS/TS plane; its own Bun workspace root: - `console/` — the console: ONE SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 single-page app with no backend of its own. The browser signs in to Dex with PKCE on the public `rask-web` client, keeps its tokens in memory under a strict Content Security Policy, and calls the catalog, lineage and inbox APIs with its bearer. A small Bun server (`serve.ts`) serves the built files and the runtime `config.json` - `packages/` — `@rask/ui` (Svelte 5 + Bits UI + Tailwind 4 design system, Storybook), `@rask/api` (the typed client generated from the OpenAPI specs), `@rask/dockview` (the workbench), `@rask/flow` (the governance graphs) - `scripts/` — all dev/ops scripts (the e2e stack drivers, the estate seed, the chart and store tooling) - `tests/` — cross-service suites: `unit`, `integration`, `e2e-py` (**live**, `-m e2e`, needs a deployed stack), `e2e` (Playwright, its own lockfile) - `chart/` — the product chart: the lakehouse's services and their configuration, with OpenFGA as its only (optional) subchart. Dapr, NATS JetStream, the CloudNativePG operator, External Secrets, Dex, the object store and observability are prerequisites, installed in development from `deploy/fixtures/` (ADR 0153) - `deploy/fixtures/console` — the console's own release: the web image, the notifications inbox and an HTTPRoute on the platform's Gateway, beside the product chart and installed after it - `.docker/` — one dockerfile per deployable; `.dagger/` — the build + CI module; `docs/` — Zensical source (the depth lives here) Workspace membership is **globbed per plane**: `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*", "services/*"]` and `frontend/package.json` `workspaces = ["console", "packages/*"]`. A new directory joins its plane automatically — provided it ships a `pyproject.toml` / `package.json`; without one it is silently skipped. Deployables build from the root lock via `uv sync --package `. ## Quick start On a new computer, `scripts/new-machine.sh` walks through all of it: the toolchain, the clone, a handover kit from the old machine (memory, `.env`, local branches), and the k3s estate installed from empty. ```bash make install # bun --cwd=frontend install + uv sync --all-packages + git hooks + make k3s-deps + make claude-bootstrap make build make test # offline suites (deselects the live `e2e` + long-running `slow` marks) make check # fmt + lint + typecheck + knip ``` ## Run locally ```bash make dev # the console with Vite HMR, /api → RASK_EDGE_URL (default :8888) make dev-k3s # the console against the in-cluster Gateway, port-forwarded to :8888 make dev-micro # the notifications inbox on the host (no edge) ``` The lakehouse services (catalog, lineage, maintenance) need Dapr, NATS, OpenFGA and an object store, so they run on k3s, and the console reaches them through the cluster's Gateway (`make dev-k3s`). ## Clusters The chart in `chart/` is the single deploy artifact for both. - **k3s** — the long-lived local/single-node deploy, and where the live estate runs: ```bash make k3s-install # one-time host bootstrap (sudo) make k3s-build k3s-import k3s-up # build, side-load, helm install + wait make k3s-clients # the console's release (web + inbox) after the lakehouse make seed-dev # projects, warehouses, namespaces and grants through the catalog make k9s # inspect it make k3s-down / k3s-purge ``` - **kind** — throwaway and CI-shaped, used by the live-proof jobs: ```bash make kind-up kind-images kind-load kind-deploy make e2e-ci # governed kind stack + the live e2e suites (== CI e2e-stack job) ``` > Both clusters can exist at once, and a bare `kubectl` may reach the **kind** one. The k3s release > lives at `KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml` — the Makefile already sets it. **Dagger builds every image — never `docker build`.** `dagger call image --name=` for anything in `.docker/` (`frontend` is the console's image, `make console-image`); `scripts/dagger-image.sh` is the single seam. The dockerfile stays the source of truth, so a build cannot behave one way locally and another in CI. ## Security scanning ```bash make audit # osv-scanner over every lockfile + .dagger/go.mod make scan-config # trivy misconfig + secret detection over dockerfiles + chart make scan-secrets # trufflehog over git history (gates on VERIFIED credentials only) make scan-image NAME=notifications ``` ## CI `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls the Dagger module's real functions — `lint`, `typecheck`, `openapi`, `test`, `charts`, `frontend`, `scan-*` — plus the kind-backed live jobs (`make e2e-ci`) and the console's Playwright suite. Everything hermetic runs identically on your machine: `dagger call ` == the CI step. ## Common Make targets | Target | What it does | | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `make install` / `make build` | Install both planes / build everything | | `make test` / `make test-slow` | pytest offline (`-m "not slow and not e2e"`) / + slow | | `make check` / `make ci` | fmt + lint + typecheck + knip / + tests | | `make dev` / `make dev-k3s` | The console with Vite HMR / against the in-cluster Gateway | | `make dev-micro` | The notifications inbox on the host | | `make console-image` | The console's image through Dagger | | `make k3s-build k3s-import k3s-up` | The long-lived k3s deploy | | `make k3s-clients` | The console's release, after the lakehouse | | `make kind-up … kind-deploy` | Throwaway kind cluster lifecycle | | `make e2e-ci` | The guarded live proofs (kind) | | `make e2e` | Playwright browser e2e against a running deploy | | `make storybook` | `@rask/ui` Storybook on `:6006` | | `make dev-gc` | Reclaim the dev loop's two disk leaks (Dagger cache + dev registry) | See the `Makefile` (`make help`) for the complete list; `docs/` carries the depth (`docs/architecture/layout.md`, `docs/architecture/deployment.md`). [uv]: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ [Bun]: https://bun.sh [Zensical]: https://zensical.com [Dagger]: https://dagger.io
